hed: U.S. marks 25 years since Sept. 11; Trump speaks at Pentagon
dek: The United States observed the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks that killed about 2,977 people at the World Trade Center, the Pentagon, and in Shanksville, Pa. President Donald Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth spoke Friday at the Pentagon ceremony; Vice President JD Vance attended the Ground Zero / National September 11 Memorial ceremony in New York with former presidents; other administration officials were at the Flight 93 National Memorial. New York’s ceremony added a seventh moment of silence for people who died later from toxic-dust illnesses. The same day, the CIA released 71 declassified President’s Daily Brief products (Feb. 1998–Sept. 12, 2001) on bin Laden and al-Qaeda threats briefed to Presidents Clinton and Bush — Director John Ratcliffe called it the agency’s largest 9/11 analysis release. Friday is also Patriot Day and a National Day of Service and Remembrance.

byline: Event summary from public reporting and named outlets

cl.body: AP, CNN, PBS NewsHour, and NBC coverage center Friday’s observances on remembrance at all three attack sites, Vance and former presidents at Ground Zero’s new toxic-dust silence, and Trump’s completed Pentagon remarks — while also noting that Trump and Hegseth used parts of the ceremony to discuss the ongoing Iran war alongside memorial language.

cr.body: NY Post, The Hill, Fox News, and Florida’s Voice / CIA statements emphasize Trump’s “That’s why we fight today” framing and Hegseth’s vigilance / Iran-as-sponsor-of-terror language at the Pentagon, plus the same-day declassification of 71 PDBs as exceptional transparency on pre-9/11 bin Laden warnings to Clinton and Bush.
